summary: Rowan County lookout on Dunn's Mountain: tree platform in 1952, steel tower in 1957, removed in 1971; the summit is now part of a public park.

facts.design: Steel tower, replacing an early 1952 tree-platform tower
facts.status_note: The county history says the summit lookout was removed in 1971.

access.note: The summit is part of an 83-acre public park with a trail and a weekend shuttle. The lookout itself is gone.

visit.trail_note: A quarter-mile trail, mostly paved, climbs to the summit. A shuttle runs to the top on weekends.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Spring 1952 platform built between two trees, with windows and a roof added later.

A 1960 recovery note by the North Carolina Division of Forestry, printed in the NGS datasheet, dates a fire tower about 10 feet from the survey mark to summer 1956. This conflicts with the county's 1952 date.
The tree tower was replaced by a steel tower.
A 1965 NGS recovery note says a fire tower stands to the north on the same hilltop, and the old log building is gone.
The county history says the Dunn's Mountain tower was removed in 1971.
The summit opened to the public as a park.
NGS recovery note places the survey mark in the gravel parking lot of the Dunn Mountain visitor center.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The county history dates the first lookout to spring 1952. A 1960 survey note dates a fire tower near the mark to summer 1956. The story uses the county date and reports the 1956 note.

sources.title: North Carolina's Once-Thriving Quarry Was Abandoned And Transformed Into A Scenic Mountain Park

notes_for_editor: Dates for the lookout come from one county history page and two NGS survey notes (1960 and 1965). The 1952 and 1956 construction dates conflict, and the story says so. Brief status unknown is now removed, based on the county's 1971 date. Park facts rest on a travel article (islands.com); the VisitNC listing returned 404. Brief coordinates match the NGS mark within about 30 m. No photos were found. Nothing in the sources says what, if anything, remains of the lookout on the summit.
